findings: Plan-implementation mismatch — The plan specifies a MongoDB-to-PostgreSQL migration with Sequelize ORM across 25 steps. The implementation ignored this plan entirely and implemented features using the existing MongoDB/Mongoose stack.

Empty Sequelize configuration — Plan step 2 calls for creating backend/config/database.js with a Sequelize instance. This file does not exist. The server.js file still uses mongoose.connect() instead of sequelize.authenticate() and sequelize.sync().

Rate limiter inconsistency — The verificationLimiter is applied at the route level in auth.js while authLimiter and withdrawalLimiter are applied globally in server.js. Either apply all three in server.js or document why verification requires route-level application.

Verification code hashing gap — The verification code (6-digit numeric string) is stored in plaintext in User.verificationCode. An attacker with read access to the database could steal verification codes and bypass phone verification. Hash the verification code before storing it.

Ledger entry type fee ambiguity — When a withdrawal is rejected, admin.js creates two entries with type withdrawal_refund (one for amount, one for fee). This overloads withdrawal_refund to mean both types of refund, making reporting ambiguous. Consider adding fee_refund to the type enum.

Transaction history lacks pagination — The transaction history endpoint (GET /users/me/transactions) returns all ledger entries for a user with no limit. Add pagination (limit, offset or cursor-based) to prevent performance degradation.

Audit log lacks timestamp filtering — The audit log endpoint (GET /admin/audit-logs) returns the 100 most recent logs with no filtering capability. For compliance and forensics, audit logs need query filters (date range, action, targetType, adminId).

Support ticket reply lacks audit trail — When an admin replies to a support ticket, the reply is stored in SupportTicket.adminReply (a single text field), but no AuditLog entry is created. The schema only supports one reply per ticket. Either create an AuditLog entry for each reply or refactor adminReply to an array.
